groups.control_summary: Sajjan Jindal's branch controls JSW Steel through a web of holding companies (JSW Techno Projects Management 10.82%, JSW Holdings 7.42%, Vividh Finvest 5.86%, Sahyog Holdings 4.58% and others); JFE Steel of Japan holds 15.00% of JSW Steel as a strategic investor. Other Jindal branches hold small promoter-group stakes in JSW Steel (Naveen Jindal, Arti and Deepika Jindal, the Jindal sisters), reflecting common O.P. Jindal ancestry rather than joint control.
groups.background: O.P. Jindal started a pipe and bends unit at Liluah near Kolkata in 1952 and later built the Jindal group in Hisar, Haryana. After his death in a 2005 helicopter crash the group was divided among his four sons: Prithviraj (Jindal Saw), Sajjan (JSW), Ratan (Jindal Stainless) and Naveen (Jindal Steel, formerly JSPL), with mother Savitri Jindal as chairperson emeritus. Sajjan Jindal moved to Mumbai and built JSW around the Vijayanagar steel works in Karnataka and the Dolvi works in Maharashtra, then added power, ports, cement and paints. Growth since 2018 has come largely through insolvency buys (Monnet Ispat, Bhushan Power & Steel) and joint ventures with JFE (electrical steel, BPSL). JSW is now India's largest steelmaker by capacity, with the decision office in Mumbai (BKC).

Novelis and Utkal Alumina are wholly owned by Hindalco; Essel Mining is a closely held group company run from Kolkata.
groups.background: The Birla family traces its business to Seth Shiv Narayan Birla's trading house in the 19th century; G.D. Birla built it into one of India's largest industrial groups. Hindalco was incorporated in 1958 and began aluminium production at Renukoot, Uttar Pradesh, in 1962. Aditya Vikram Birla expanded the group in India and South-East Asia; after his death in 1995 Kumar Mangalam Birla, then 28, took over and added copper (Birla Copper, Dahej), Indal, Novelis (2007) and the Utkal Alumina refinery in Odisha. The wider Birla family split in the 1980s into separate lines (B.K., K.K., C.K., M.P. and the Aditya Birla line); the K.K. Bangur and other Birla-related groups are separate.

groups.control_summary: Tata Trusts own about 66% of Tata Sons, which is the promoter of Tata Steel; the Shapoorji Pallonji (Mistry) family holds about 18.4% of Tata Sons, and Tata operating companies about 13%. The SP group is pushing for a Tata Sons listing and a partial monetisation; the Trusts oppose listing (2026, reported).
groups.background: Tata Steel was set up in 1907 at Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, as Asia's first integrated private steel plant. It grew in India and abroad (Corus, 2007), then consolidated in India with Bhushan Steel (2018, IBC), Usha Martin's steel business (2019) and Neelachal Ispat Nigam (2022). Between 2023 and 2025 it merged most listed and unlisted subsidiaries into itself, and in 2025-26 it bought out BlueScope's half of the coated-steel venture. Control sits with Tata Sons and, behind it, the Tata Trusts; there is no family promoter in the usual sense.

groups.background: B.K. Goenka and his cousin Rajesh Mandawewala started Welspun in 1985 with textiles and moved into large-diameter line pipes in the 1990s from Gujarat (Anjar, Dahej). Welspun Corp became one of the world's larger welded-pipe makers with plants in India, the USA (Little Rock) and a Saudi associate (EPIC). It has since moved upstream into plates, coils and DI pipes (Welspun Metallics, Anjar) and specialty stainless (Welspun Specialty Solutions, Jhagadia), and bought Sintex BAPL. The group also runs Welspun Living (home textiles), Welspun Enterprises (infrastructure) and warehousing.

groups.background: The Gupta brothers and B.L. Agarwal built the Lloyds group around Lloyds Steel at Wardha (later sold to Uttam Galva) and a sponge iron and power unit at Ghugus, Chandrapur. Lloyds Metals won the Surjagarh iron ore lease in Gadchiroli in 2007, but mining was stalled for years by Maoist violence. Thriveni Earthmovers of Salem, Tamil Nadu (B. Prabhakaran) came in as mine developer-operator and shareholder, and Surjagarh output was scaled up rapidly after 2021. The group is now building pellet, DRI and steel capacity at Konsari and Hedri in Gadchiroli and is one of Maharashtra's largest recent investors in the district.

groups.background: Mukand began in Lahore in 1929 and was acquired by Jamnalal Bajaj and Jivanlal Shah at Mahatma Gandhi's urging; it moved to Mumbai and opened the Kalwe steel plant near Thane in 1965. Management alternated between the Bajaj and Shah families (Kamalnayan Bajaj, Viren Shah, Rahul Bajaj, then Niraj Bajaj with Rajesh Shah from 2007). In 2019 the alloy steel business at Hospet, Karnataka, moved to Mukand Sumi Special Steel, a joint venture of Jamnalal Sons and Sumitomo; Mukand Ltd now focuses on stainless and alloy long products at Kalwe. Hospet Steels is a long-standing joint venture with the Kalyani group (Kalyani Mukand Ltd is a related party).

groups.control_summary: Baba Kalyani's family controls Bharat Forge, Kalyani Steels and BF Utilities through promoter investment companies; Kalyani Technoforge is 100% held by promoter investment holding companies and Saarloha is wholly owned by the group since buying out Carpenter Technology in FY2016. Kalyani Forge is a separate listed company of brother G.N. (Gaurishankar) Kalyani's family.
groups.background: Neelkanth Rao Kalyani, an agriculturist-turned-industrialist from the Karad area, incorporated Bharat Forge in Pune on 19 June 1961. His elder son Baba Kalyani turned it into one of the world's largest forging companies from the 1990s, with plants in Germany, Sweden, France and the USA, and later added defence and aerospace. Kalyani Steels (1973) and Saarloha (special steel, 1998 JV with Carpenter) were set up as backward integration and today supply about half of Bharat Forge's steel; Kalyani Technoforge (1979) does forging and machining around Pune. Since 2023 the family has been in a high-value inheritance dispute with Baba's sister Sugandha Hiremath and her family, now under Supreme Court-appointed mediation.

groups.background: The Kirloskar group began in 1888 when Laxmanrao Kirloskar started making ploughs; his son Shantanurao built engines and electricals businesses after 1946. Shantanurao's son Chandrakant had three sons, Sanjay, Atul and Rahul, who are brothers (not cousins); Shrikant's son Vikram (d. 2022) ran Toyota Kirloskar. Under a 2009 deed of family settlement Sanjay took Kirloskar Brothers, Atul took Kirloskar Oil Engines and Rahul took Kirloskar Pneumatic. Kirloskar Ferrous, the metals arm held through Kirloskar Industries, makes pig iron and castings at Koppal in Karnataka and bought ISMT (seamless tubes) in 2022, merging it in 2024.

Triggered by Atul and Rahul's 2017 purchase of La Gajjar Machineries (a pump maker competing with KBL); about 40 cases including NCLT oppression petitions, arbitration, the 'Kirloskar' trademark (Pune court relief to KBL, Feb 2025) and SEBI's order to disclose the deed (KOEL appeal to SAT; Bombay High Court challenge by five companies). groups.background: Basant Lall Shaw founded the NECO group in Nagpur in 1972 as a foundry and grew it into one of India's larger castings makers. From 1996 the group built an integrated steel plant at Siltara, Raipur, Chhattisgarh (blast furnace, DRI, coke oven, power); some units were first set up under Abhijeet Infrastructures Ltd and the company was renamed Jayaswal Neco Industries in 2007. In 2008 the Abhijeet group, led by Manoj Jayaswal, separated from the parent (reported). In 2023 Basant Lall Shaw became Chairman Emeritus and his sons Arvind and Ramesh took the chairman and MD roles; grandsons Anand and Avneesh joined the board in January 2026.
